**Owner request (2026-11-21):** four threads, each in its own worktree, each first proposes an ADR that I review; I send GREENLIGHT; then each thread implements via GPT-6.1 Terra (high) sub-agents (`delegate_task`, codex `gpt-6.1-terra`) and reviews it before asking me to review. My review must include screenshots and videos where applicable. ADR for Android sign-in must be NEW, not an edit of ADR 0001.

**Owner answers:** ADRs all in parallel, implementation at most 2 tracks at a time (my proposed order: A + C first, then B, then D, since D's Android part needs B). **Merge: each track PRs to `main` and I (Claude) merge after my review + CI** (explicit owner choice). Desktop send = macOS only. Cleared `target/debug/incremental` (disk was 5.2 GB free → 8.4 GB).

**Tracks** (rules: `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/RULES.md`; emulator lock `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/emulator.lock`):
- A install/signing/ANR/package ID — ADR 0004, `usable/install`, codex gpt-6.2-sol high, thread `mcp:launch:573c8819…`
- B Google sign-in on Android — ADR 0005, `usable/android-gmail`, claude-opus-5-5 high, thread `mcp:launch:ab75b75b…`
- C HTML display — ADR 0006, `usable/html-reader`, claude-opus-5-5 high, thread `mcp:launch:33fa7c62…`
- D sending (macOS + Android) — ADR 0007, `usable/send`, codex gpt-6.2-sol high (owner gave no effort; I chose high), thread `mcp:launch:7bb2a69a…`

- ADR 0003 (mobile layout) already existed on main, so tracks use 0004–0007 (threads steered 13:33 UTC; thread titles still show the old numbers). My local `main` checkout is stale (f605bc1); always look at `origin/main`.

**Owner decisions on the ADRs (2026-11-21, ~13:45 UTC):** app ID `dev.exedev.emailos` ("Email OS"); phone has Play services (model/Android version not yet given); send = **Undo send for a few seconds, no confirmation dialog** (I set 5 s; overrides their earlier "quiet endings" for this one case); Android first run = choice screen (your mail / demo); signing key on the owner's own computer + protected GitHub environment, never on the VM; delivery = **GitHub Releases** (repo is public); Disconnect = local only; "Load images" = this message only.

B (0005 @ 51f2ae5) and D (0007 @ 0900cce) approved but told to stay idle until I send `START`. content.text:
I reproduced the swipe-to-done bug and fixed it. The fix isn't committed. The branch is `fix-swipe-mark-done` with the changes in the working tree. I haven't tried it on the Android emulator.

**The bug:** when you swipe a row to mark it done, the row slides off screen. It then snaps back to its normal position and stays fully visible until the archive finishes, and only then disappears.

I reproduced this in real Chromium, driven with touch events. I added 600 ms of delay to the fake archive call and sampled the row's position every 40 ms:
- **Before the fix:** the row slid out to about −340 px, snapped back to 0 at ~250 ms, and stayed visible until ~870 ms.
- **After the fix:** it stays off screen until the backend call finishes and the row is gone.

The fixture normally answers instantly, which is why the existing test never caught this. With a real Gmail account the call takes longer, so the flash would be longer too.

**Cause:** the swipe reset the row's position about one frame after it committed. The row only leaves the list after the archive call and a list refresh complete (`submitMutation` in `useMailbox.ts`).

**The fix:**
- **Hold the row:** `useSwipeAction` now lets a commit return a promise. The row stays slid out and keeps its coloured "Mark done" fill until that promise settles.
- **Row gone:** the state resets without animation. Because the reset also clears the stale state, Undo brings the row back at rest instead of slid out.
- **Row still listed:** if the archive failed or was refused, the row springs back with animation.
- **Cancelled gesture:** a late result from a cancelled gesture is ignored.
- **Wiring:** `InboxList.vue` waits for the in-flight command on that row via a new `pendingRef` prop. `App.vue` passes it `mailbox.inFlightCommandRef`.

**Tests:**
- I added tests for the composable (hold, spring-back, cancel) and for the list component (hold, Undo restore, spring-back).
- The full suite passes (2347 tests), typecheck is clean, and the rendered mobile list and pages tests pass in Chromium.
- The rendered test's fake has no latency, so no automated test covers the original slow-backend symptom. I only saw it with a temporary delay, which I reverted.

I also ran `pnpm install` in this worktree, because the shared `node_modules` was stale and lacked `dompurify`. `node_modules` isn't tracked, so nothing from that shows up in git.

Here's the side-by-side recording. Both sides run the same swipe in real Chromium at phone size, with the backend call slowed to 1 s to stand in for a real Gmail round trip.

![Before and after the swipe fix](/tmp/claude-1000/-home-exedev--t3-worktrees-email-os-4a2825cf-bd9fbd8bf5e16c35/2d22a962-0e1c-4870-b64e-39c50a032a77/scratchpad/before-after.mp4)

File: `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-exedev--t3-worktrees-email-os-4a2825cf-bd9fbd8bf5e16c35/2d22a962-0e1c-4870-b64e-39c50a032a77/scratchpad/before-after.mp4`

A contact sheet of frames from the video shows the difference. The red dot is a finger marker I injected for the recording.
- **Both sides:** the row is dragged left past the threshold, the purple "Mark done" fill appears, and the row slides off screen.
- **Left, old code:** the "Archive Fixture" row snaps back into place, fully visible, while the archive is still pending. The "Mark done" fill disappears with it. The row only goes when the backend answers, after which the "Mark done · Oversized HTML sample" notice with Undo appears.
- **Right, new code:** the "Mark done" fill stays on screen through the whole wait. When the archive finishes, the row is gone and the Undo notice appears. The row never flashes back.

The video uses the fixture backend and an artificial 1 s delay, not a real Gmail account, and I haven't run it on the Android emulator. It sits in the session scratchpad, so copy it somewhere permanent if you want to keep it. The recording scaffolding and the latency patch are removed, so the working tree again holds only the fix and its tests.
